steps.name: TF activity from the aldosterone contrast (decoupleR + CollecTRI)
caveats: A prior network is tissue-agnostic: a kidney-specific regulator with few curated targets can be missed, and targets silent in kidney add noise. State this beside the results

An inferred activity is a statement about the coordinated behaviour of curated targets, not a measurement of TF protein abundance or binding
Unsigned resources such as the MSigDB C3 GTRD target sets cannot express direction and are not a substitute for a signed regulon
steps.context: Human kidney, aldosterone vs vehicle. Aldosterone acts through the mineralocorticoid receptor (NR3C2, with NR3C1 cross-talk), so canonical early-response targets — SGK1, SCNN1A/B/G, FKBP5, TSC22D3, PER1 — are a biological positive control for whether the contrast captured the intended perturbation. Only 12 samples exist, which is far too few to infer a regulatory network from the expression itself, so a prior knowledge network is the only defensible source of regulons.
steps.question: Which transcription factors show altered inferred activity in aldosterone-treated versus vehicle-control kidney samples, based on the coordinated behaviour of their curated target genes?

grounding.reason: TF activity from a contrast: decoupleR ulm on the Wald statistic of all tested genes with the signed CollecTRI human regulons (R-0111@b668); DoRothEA A-C is the stated fallback (R-0113@7a4d); a 12-sample cohort forbids expression-derived network inference (R-0121@5f27).

constraints: Run decoupleR ulm on the Wald statistic of all tested genes from T1S2; do not restrict the input to significant genes
Use a human regulon network — never the mouse or rat resource — and keep the signed mode of regulation on each edge
Minimum regulon size 5 targets present among the tested genes
Adjust TF p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg and report the adjusted values alongside the raw
Do not infer a regulatory network from this 12-sample expression matrix; the prior network is the only permitted source of regulons, and state this in the output

steps.description: Infer transcription-factor activity from the T1S2 contrast statistic using the decoupleR univariate linear model (ulm). Input is the Wald statistic of EVERY tested gene from T1S2 — not the significant subset. plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level Salmon count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 human kidney samples, gene symbols in the first column) with a metadata table giving one condition per sample: 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle controls, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which transcription factors sit behind the change — so the plan is a short linear chain plus a robustness check.

T1S1 does sample-structure QC before any model: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, coloured by condition. With n=6 per group a single mislabelled or outlying sample can dominate the contrast, and this is the only place it is visible before testing. T1S2 fits the model that the design supports: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors inside the negative-binomial model (no pre-scaled counts), an explicit reference level of the vehicle/control group so a positive log2 fold change means higher in aldosterone-treated, DESeq2 Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for ranking, BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, and the p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment. Because the counts came from Salmon, the length-offset route (tximport) is the correct import — but only a summarised gene-level matrix is provided here, so the step must state that no length offsets are available and that a gene with an isoform-usage shift can therefore be mis-called. At 6 vs 6, DESeq2 flags rather than replaces count outliers, so genes with NA p-values must be reported separately from those the independent filter removed.

T1S3 runs edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same counts and design as an independent robustness check; the intersection is the high-confidence gene set and the union is not the result. T2S1 answers the second half of the question: TF activity by decoupleR univariate linear model on the CollecTRI human signed regulons, taking the Wald statistic of every tested gene (not the significant subset), keeping the mode of regulation so repressor targets lower the score, and requiring at least 5 targets present. A prior network is the only defensible source of regulons here — 12 samples cannot support an expression-derived network — and CollecTRI is tissue-agnostic, so a kidney-specific regulator with few curated targets can be missed. Known aldosterone/mineralocorticoid biology (NR3C1/NR3C2 and their canonical targets SGK1, SCNN1A/B/G, FKBP5, TSC22D3, PER1) is a positive control to report against, not a filter. T2S2 assembles the reproducibility report.

The design is clean: balanced, unpaired, single batch, no covariates, so no batch or confounding correction is warranted and none is planned. Power at 6 vs 6 is moderate — a null result for a given gene is not evidence of no effect, and this must be stated rather than glossed.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples
~ condition with control as explicit reference level; contrast condition treated vs control
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected
decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI human regulons using the DESeq2 Wald statistic of all tested genes
Reproducibility report: MA plot, dispersion plot, thresholds, counts of DE genes, edgeR QL overlap, sessionInfo

An explicit statement of whether NR3C1/NR3C2 and the canonical aldosterone-response genes (SGK1, SCNN1A/B/G, FKBP5, TSC22D3, PER1) are present among the tested genes and what their contrast statistics were — reported as a positive control, not used to filter results
constraints: Run decoupleR ulm on the Wald statistic of all tested genes from T1S2; do not restrict the input to significant genes
Use a human regulon network — never the mouse or rat resource — and keep the signed mode of regulation on each edge
Minimum regulon size 5 targets present among the tested genes
Adjust TF p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg and report the adjusted values alongside the raw
Do not infer a regulatory network from this 12-sample expression matrix; the prior network is the only permitted source of regulons, and state this in the output
If neither the CollecTRI nor the DoRothEA human regulon resource can be resolved in the environment, stop and report that rather than substituting an unsigned TF-target set
caveats: A prior network is tissue-agnostic: a kidney-specific regulator with few curated targets can be missed, and targets silent in kidney add noise. State this beside the results
VIPER on an ARACNe regulon is the tool of record for a context-specific regulator activity and is not available here; decoupleR on a prior network is the substitute
An inferred activity is a statement about the coordinated behaviour of curated targets, not a measurement of TF protein abundance or binding
Unsigned resources such as the MSigDB C3 GTRD target sets cannot express direction and are not a substitute for a signed regulon

steps.name: Consolidated report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the complete, reproducible account of the aldosterone-vs-vehicle kidney differential expression result and the transcription factors inferred behind it?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. State the method and package versions, the design formula ~ condition, the contrast (condition: aldosterone-treated vs vehicle control) and its reference level, the thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering on), the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000, and the number of DE genes up and down. Carry the fit diagnostics before the gene tables: the MA plot on the shrunken fold changes and the dispersion-estimate plot, plus the p-value histogram. Present the gene table ranked by the shrunken log2 fold change, showing the unshrunken estimate, the shrunken estimate and the lfcSE side by side. Include the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the robustness statement and the TF activity table with its regulon source and version. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, any random seed, and the version of the regulon collection used.
steps.context: Final synthesis across both tracks. Everything reported here must trace to an artifact produced by an upstream step — no number is to be restated from memory or estimated.
acceptance_criteria: Report states method, package versions, design formula, contrast with its reference level, thresholds, number of genes tested and number of DE genes up and down
MA plot on shrunken fold changes, dispersion plot and p-value histogram appear before the gene tables
Gene table gives unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE per gene, ranked by the shrunken value
DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap reported as the robustness statement, with the intersection identified as the high-confidence set
TF activity results included with the regulon resource name and version stated
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seed and regulon collection version written alongside the results
Power limitation at 6 vs 6 stated explicitly, and the missing Salmon length-offset limitation carried forward from T1S2
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit and name the shrinkage estimator in the table header
Report the two NA causes separately: Cook's-distance outlier flag versus independent filtering
Do not restate any number that is not present in an upstream artifact
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
caveats: An inferred TF activity is a hypothesis about upstream regulation, not a measured mechanism; keep interpretation at that level
Aldosterone-response biology should be reported as consistent or inconsistent with the result, never used to select which results are shown

grounding.reason: Report content, the shrunken/unshrunken effect columns, the MA and dispersion diagnostics, the two-method overlap and the reproducibility record follow R-0041, R-0085, R-0087, R-0042 and R-0086.
